Reverse shell communication instead of bind shell
Commands sent dynamically by C2 server instead of hardcoded

Attaches BPF to sniff UDP, TCP, SCTP traffic on ports 22, 80, 443
Forks process to connect to C2 server and establish reverse shell
Ignores OS signals to avoid interruption
Removes reliance on external libraries for encryption to improve stealth
Avoids detection by signature-based antivirus by removing hardcoded commands

Reverse shell connection from infected host to attacker C2 server
Exploitation of 2019 vulnerability for persistence (reported by CrowdStrike)
